prompt: What is the degree of the polynomial $(x^2 + 1)(x^3 - 2)$ when it is fully expanded?
hint: You do not need to expand — the degrees combine.

hints.text: You do not need to expand — the degrees combine.
The highest-degree term comes from multiplying the two leading terms: $x^2 \cdot x^3$.

learningObjective: Determine the degree of a product of polynomials.
explanation: When polynomials are multiplied, their degrees add.
The first factor has degree $2$ and the second has degree $3$, so the product has degree $5$.
Confirming by expansion: $x^5 - 2x^2 + x^3 - 2$, whose highest power is indeed $x^5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Only the leading terms matter
steps: Every other product produces a lower power, so it cannot affect the degree.
Multiply just the leading terms — $x^2 \cdot x^3 = x^5$ — and stop there.
The same shortcut answers "what is the leading coefficient" questions: multiply just the leading coefficients.
